trigger: A hand-edited violating sessions row already cached by a peer replica when the v2 migration deletes it; the peer keeps serving it until some unrelated write bumps write_generation (a healthy refresh sees an unchanged generation, the 30 s stale bound covers refresh outages only).
summary: The v2 migration DELETE removes rows without bumping session_store.session_meta write_generation, so a peer replica keeps a deleted session cached. Gate 2 security-guardian labelled it NICE (E6-leaning); authdb derived HIGH (I1 base, E5, E6 not provable); architect rated the bump optional. Recorded at the derived band.
classification_rationale: Native NICE vs derived HIGH disagreed; the derived band governs the gate. Fixed rather than adjudicated down.

trigger: A hand-edited violating row exists at upgrade; the migration deletes it, forcing that principal to sign in again, with no row count logged, audited or exposed as a metric.
summary: CC6.2/CC6.8: the migration DELETE is a forced sign-out that leaves no evidence. Compliance labelled it native MEDIUM; the nominal derivation (I1 base HIGH, E5) is HIGH, recorded at that band.
classification_rationale: Missing runtime record of a revocation-by-migration; fixed by emitting and documenting the count.

trigger: An operator or security-questionnaire reader relies on docs/user-manual/security-hardening.md saying session tokens have no durable storage and that a restart revokes every session.
summary: The page says sessions are in-memory only and a restart is a fleet-wide revocation; SessionStore (HA WS-1/1a) persists them and a restart does not revoke. Derived HIGH (I4/I3, E3); pre-existing, the orchestrator ruled to fix it in this PR because the commit already touches the session store.
classification_rationale: A false control statement in an operator/assurance document.

trigger: At least one violating row exists and its principal issues a session write (create/touch/elevate) between the migration DELETE and the ALTER; a second replica or rolling upgrade widens the window.
summary: The v2 DELETE (row locks) followed by the ALTER (lock upgrade to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE) deadlocks with a live session writer waiting on a deleted row (reproduced on postgres:18); a row committed between the two would also fail the ADD validation and refuse boot. Retry-safe (full rollback).
classification_rationale: Found at Gate 8 pass 1 in the fix round; the original 5be5d0a94 had the same DELETE-then-ALTER shape.

trigger: A new replica boots while pg_dump or another long transaction holds a lock on sessions; the queued ACCESS EXCLUSIVE request makes every later sessions query on running peers wait up to the lock_timeout, repeated by a crash-looping supervisor; unbounded when a DSN options/PGOPTIONS setting suppresses the pool timeouts.
summary: The queued table lock stalls peers for the pool lock_timeout (10 s) per attempt, or without bound when the DSN sets its own options.
classification_rationale: Gate 8 pass 1 unhappy-path R2-1; the pre-lock ALTER had the same exposure, so the exposure is not new, only now stated and bounded.

trigger: An operator pre-applies a constraint named sessions_principal_kind_consistent while schema_meta is still at 1; v2 ADD CONSTRAINT then fails 42710 and refuses boot on every restart with no remediation text.
summary: ADD CONSTRAINT is not idempotent against a hand-applied same-name constraint.
classification_rationale: Gate 4 UP-2.

trigger: A future edit reverts one of the changed engine-classification sites to the raw stored-kind compare.
summary: Only audit_log_for_session had a split-state regression test; require_permission, require_scoped_permission, require_list_read, require_fleet_read, make_audit_event, both MCP stream .cls stamps had none. Ordinary missing coverage stays SHOULD.
classification_rationale: Quality-engineer QE-1 found the cold-cache AuthManager + cookie seam that makes a split session injectable.
